title: Where Can the Mind Go?
hookLine: a book of focus asks where a wandering mind could possibly go
carry: shiva is everywhere, so the mind can't leave
tomorrow: a sacred book says to savor your food. a door, or a detour?
last: THE SAME KNOWING IN EVERY SEAT.

cards: Ninety seconds into a quiet sit, the mind has left the building. A quiz on Thursday. A text left on read.
A chorus from middle school, on repeat. Then comes the sinking feeling, the one that says this is hopeless, I can't even sit still. So where exactly did it go?

Here's the odd detail. The Vijnana Bhairava is a book of ways to steady the attention, and one of its verses asks that very question, then answers it with a puzzle of its own: where could the mind possibly go?

teach.b: The verse runs like this, in plain words. Wherever the mind goes, outward or inward, there is Shiva's own state. And since he is everywhere, where can the mind go?
The Sanskrit for that roaming mind is manas: the part that plans, replays and drifts. Now the puzzle.

teach.h: THE OTHER DOORS SAY STAY PUT.
teach.b: The doors so far ask the attention to stay put: rest at the turn of the breath, follow a sound to its end, catch a want at its flicker. This one lets the mind off the leash and follows it out.
Why would a book of focus do that? Because of the story it sits in. When the Goddess asked Bhairava what he really is, he told her his nature can't be pinned to any place or direction.
Here's the teaching under that, named plainly: for this tradition, God is all-pervading, present in everything and outside nothing.

teach.h: ISHA: ALL THIS, DWELT IN BY THE LORD.
teach.b: The Isha Upanishad opens the same way: all this, whatever moves in the world, is to be dwelt in by the Lord. If that's so, there's no outside to wander into.
The quiz, the unanswered text, the old chorus: none of them, in the book's view, is somewhere God isn't. That doesn't make wandering the goal. It changes what noticing it means.
The moment you see the mind has gone somewhere isn't a failure. It's the moment you woke up there, and found the Lord there too.

teach.h: SHIVA IS EVERYWHERE; THE MIND CAN'T LEAVE.
teach.b: So the puzzle solves itself: the mind can wander, but it can't leave.

how: Readers of the Vijnana Bhairava sit with one dharana at a time; with this one, they let the mind move and keep recognizing awareness wherever it lands, instead of forcing it back.

o: a manual that scolds the mind for drifting in a sit
a list of rules for sitting perfectly still in a temple
a book of doors; here, the wandering mind can't leave

games.q: the wandering-mind verse — tap the pairs.
p: a waking up, not a failure

s: real meditation means the mind never wanders
this verse follows the wandering mind and finds Shiva's state wherever it goes.
the verse asks where the mind could go, since Shiva is everywhere
its answer to drifting is a question, not a scolding.
the verse makes wandering the goal of the practice
it changes what wandering means: noticing where the mind has gone is the waking up.

games.q: your cousin says he quit meditating because his mind 'won't shut up.' what would this verse say to him?
o: the drifting isn't outside the practice; noticing it is waking up.
keep forcing it back; the mind has to be held perfectly still.
stop for now; some minds just aren't built for this kind of thing.
games.why: wherever the mind goes, the verse says, there is Shiva's state. there's no outside to drift into; seeing where it went is already the practice.

practice: Close your eyes and let the mind go wherever it likes, without herding it. Each time you notice where it's landed, don't drag it back; just recognize that you're aware there too, and let that recognition be the whole practice.

wordCard.voice: The Vijnana Bhairava: a book of doors. In this verse, a book that says the wandering mind has nowhere outside to go.
